subject: Replay ingest charge allocation — request for review and provisional credit
messages:
From: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acme-corp.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-10-12T09:11:00-04:00
Subject: Sudden usage spike Oct 10–11 — possible replay/backfill from our pipeline

Hi Priya,

We noticed a ~42% jump in billed usage for our embeddings + streaming endpoints on Oct 10–11 and are trying to understand whether this was caused by our backfill/replay job that ran over that window. Our SREs believe a retry-loop in our ingestion pipeline replayed a subset of payloads after a temporary network partition.

Two quick asks: can you confirm whether those duplicate requests were billed as unique tokens on your side, and if so how we should request an adjustment? I attached a small sample (acme-sample-telemetry.csv) with our request_ids and timestamps.

We also need to know how VAT will be handled if a credit is applied (we’re in Spain; reverse-charge may apply). We’re on the annual committed plan (deal ACME-2024-04-RENEWAL).

Can you advise next steps? This is blocking our finance team from accepting the October invoice.

Thanks —
Lina Gomez
Head of Platform Operations
Acme Corporation

Attachment: acme-sample-telemetry.csv (CSV, 120 rows sample)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acme-corp.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-12T10:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Sudden usage spike Oct 10–11 — possible replay/backfill from our pipeline

Hi Lina — thanks for the sample and the heads up.

Immediate plan: 1) I’ve asked our platform team to pull matching telemetry for the request_ids you sent so we can confirm duplication on our side; 2) I’ve looped in Kimberly (billing) to hold the Oct invoice while we investigate and Marcus (platform) for technical analysis.

Please expect a short checklist from us:
- A set of raw request_ids/timestamps (you provided a sample; we may ask for a second slice)
- Any upstream retry configuration details (retry count/backoff) you can share
- Confirmation of which project/API key should bear the valid usage

As a courtesy, we can provisionally put the Oct invoice on hold and issue a provisional credit if we verify duplicate billing. We’ll confirm VAT treatment with our tax team (since you’re in Spain we usually handle EU VAT per the reverse-charge rules but will confirm).

I’ll follow up within 48 hours with findings.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-12T10:08:00-04:00
Subject: Fwd: Sudden usage spike Oct 10–11 — ACME sample attached (please investigate)

Forwarding ACME’s sample. TL;DR: customer reports a backfill/replay that may have caused duplicate billing across embeddings and streaming. They’ve attached request_ids. Can Platform confirm whether we saw duplicate request_ids and how many unique tokens to credit? Also please flag whether attribution is to the same API key or to a replayed job that used different project metadata.

Kimberly: can you hold the Oct invoice pending Platform’s short investigation? If we need to apply a provisional credit we should discuss scale and VAT treatment.

Thanks —
Priya

On 2026-10-12 09:11, Lina Gomez wrote:
> [original message and attachment omitted]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-13T14:20:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden usage spike Oct 10–11 — ACME sample attached (please investigate)

Hi team — quick technical findings from our initial pull:

- We matched ~2,700 request_ids from ACME’s sample to our ingest logs for Oct 10–11. Of those, ~2,600 are exact duplicates where the same request_id appears 2–3x due to a client-side retry window. All duplicates were billed as separate requests in our billing pipeline because the request_id is not currently used to deduplicate billing for streaming + embeddings endpoints.
- Total billed tokens attributable to the duplicates in the sample: 1,840,300 tokens. Projecting to the full replay window (using ACME’s submitted job size) we estimate ~12.4M duplicated tokens.

Credit suggestion: based on ACME’s committed rate and our per-token price ladder, a fair provisional credit would be EUR 6,500 (net of VAT). This covers the duplicated token volume we can confidently attribute to a replay.

Technical remediation note: we can add a short-term attribution rule to deduplicate by request_id for 72 hours of retrospective matching for impacted customers; longer-term we should surface a dedupe toggle on Dedicated/Private deployments.

I’ve attached a small telemetry snippet (redwood-telemetry-snippet.json) showing matched request_ids and token counts.

—Marcus
Staff Software Engineer, Platform
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-telemetry-snippet.json (JSON, 1.2KB)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acme-corp.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-14T15:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Sudden usage spike Oct 10–11 — confirmation of provisional credit and invoice update

Hi Lina — thanks for your patience. Quick summary and next steps: 

- Platform confirmed duplicate billing tied to retries; we estimate ~12.4M duplicated tokens for the full window and propose a provisional credit of EUR 6,500 (net of VAT).
- We have placed the October invoice on hold while you review. I’ve attached the updated invoice (invoice-202610-updated.pdf) showing the provisional credit as a line item; the invoice link is: https://redwood.app/invoices/ACME-2026-10-09
- VAT treatment: because Acme is registered in Spain and has provided a valid VAT ID, we will apply the reverse-charge mechanism. The provisional credit will be issued net of VAT; final tax handling will be reconciled once the credit is accepted and we receive a signed confirmation.

Action items for Acme:
1) Confirm acceptance of the provisional credit and whether you prefer a credit on the existing invoice or a standalone credit memo.
2) Share any additional request_id slices if you want us to widen the matching window (we matched what you sent and extrapolated).
3) If you accept, provide a signed acknowledgement (simple email OK) and we’ll finalize accounting entries and issue the adjusted invoice.

If you’d like a short call to walk through the telemetry and the calculations I can coordinate with Marcus and Kimberly — otherwise we can proceed by email.

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com

Attachment: invoice-202610-updated.pdf (PDF, stub)
